text:
lee: noticed during today's canary that our SAST pipeline flagged a low-severity crypto mishandling in image-builder: pkg/crypto/keys.go: possible ignored error on Decrypt. Also our KMS audit dashboard shows fewer Decrypt events than expected for that timeframe.

pat: can you share the pod identity + time window? I'll check IAM bindings and logs.

lee: window ~1732109800-1732109860, pod svc-image-builder-canary-5b6d, SA=svc-image-builder-ephemeral.

maya: ops-bot: applied deploy 2026.04.01-canary -> status=success

ops-bot: deploy finished: svc=image-builder-canary, version=2026.04.01-11a9, tasks=6

pat: queried audit logs for Decrypt in that window, zero hits for svc-image-builder-ephemeral. There are earlier hits from svc-image-builder-prod though.

lee: odd. Could be SA drift or we fell back to cached plaintext. Either is bad.

oncall-sec: suggest capturing: pod describe, node identity, and the KMS key IAM policy. Also escalate SAST finding to the image team to confirm error handling.

maya: kubectl output: pod uses serviceAccountName: svc-image-builder-ephemeral. IAM policy for key 'prod-crypto' shows decrypter role bound to svc-image-builder-prod only. That explains missing Decrypt logs.

pat: ok, mitigation options: 1) patch canary to use prod SA, 2) add ephemeral SA to key policy (short lived), or 3) change build to avoid decrypt during canary. Which is acceptable?

lee: prefer (1) for observability parity, but we merged a narrower binding last week intentionally. Confirm with infra.

maya: I will patch the deployment to set explicit SA to svc-image-builder-prod for canary and monitor.

pat: also file SEC-2042 to track SAST triage and the RBAC change. Include the audit query and pod YAML.

oncall-sec: monitoring KMS logs now. If we see Decrypt entries after patch, close.

maya: patch applied, rolling 1/2 pods.

pat: seeing Decrypt events from svc-image-builder-prod at 1732109895. Good.

lee: assigning SAST item to @image-team to validate error handling and ensure Decrypt failures are surfaced. Closing thread and moving follow-ups to SEC-2042. :thumbsup:
